current_step_3_1: 3.1 (Quadratic residual.) Fix the nonempty compact $K$ and $L>0$. Let $b_j$ be the supremum over $K$ of the maximum absolute value of the order-$j$ component derivatives of $h$, for $j=0,1,2$; these numbers are finite by [F4]. The quantity in clause (c) is $M_K=b_0+L^{-1}b_1+L^{-2}b_2$, while the supplier's control is $B_K(h)=b_0+Lb_1+L^2b_2$. Set $q_L:=\max\{1,L^2,L^4\}$. Termwise comparison gives $B_K(h)\le q_LM_K$ for every $L>0$. Take $\delta_0,C$ from [F5] for this nonempty $K$ and $L$, and choose $\lambda_0>0$ with $\lambda_0B_K(h)\le\delta_0$ and, when $M>0$, $\lambda_0<1/(2M)$; if $B_K(h)=0$, its constraint is automatic. For $|\lambda|\le\lambda_0$, put $A=\lambda h$, so $B_K(A)=|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0$. The metric is Lorentzian on all of $\mathbb R^4$ by step 1.1. Applying the residual estimate of [F5] on $K$ gives $|G_{ab}(\eta+\lambda h)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(\lambda h)(p)|\le C\lambda^2B_K(h)^2/L^2\le Cq_L^2\lambda^2M_K^2/L^2$. By linearity and step 2.1, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(\lambda h)=\lambda G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$. Thus clause (c) holds with $C_K:=Cq_L^2<\infty$, also when $M_K=0$. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]
